\title{Conditional Work Bounds and Timing Evidence for an Industrial \ndt{} Scan Matcher:\\
Cross-Language Work-Trace Conformance}

\author{%
  \IEEEauthorblockN{Yuuki Takano}
  \IEEEauthorblockA{TIER IV, Inc.}
}

\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
Normal Distributions Transform (\ndt) scan matching has strongly input-dependent execution
time on the localization critical path. We study the align kernel of Autoware's production
matcher; map loading, preprocessing, and Robot Operating System scheduling are outside the
timed scope. Our three-layer method enforces and property-tests a conditional structural work
envelope, constructs stress witnesses with deterministic Rust counters, and measures frozen
witnesses. It separates algorithmic work from platform time and does not claim a certified
hard time bound.

A domain-informed construction attains the configured ceiling for the language-common
kernel-evaluation term; two archived candidates exercise higher Rust-specific kd-tree
traversal at lower common work. Per-input traces define \emph{work-trace conformance} over
passes, processed points, neighbor counts, and leaf identities. Leaf payloads,
implementation-specific traversal, total work, and latency remain outside that relation, so
C++ results are observations over transferred fixtures rather than a C++ worst-case search.
An auxiliary cropped-map, degraded-prior replay exposes the remaining conformance boundary.

In a unified three-boot synthetic campaign, the largest observed values are
\SI{\unifiedFixtureMaxCpp}{ms} for C++ and \SI{\unifiedFixtureMaxRust}{ms} for Rust; Rust
has the smaller maximum on all \tailsRustFasterCount{} paired fixtures. On
neighbor-returning fixtures, C++ performs approximately \allocPerPtPass{} heap allocations
per point per derivative pass, whereas the Rust align path allocates none within its reserved
envelope. Rust narrows the safe-core verification surface but is not required for bounded
execution; its unsafe code, foreign-function interface, and dependencies remain trusted.
\end{abstract}

\begin{IEEEkeywords}
timing evidence, structural work bounds, Rust, scan matching, NDT, autonomous driving,
localization
\end{IEEEkeywords}
